May 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts

records.f: 4th Utility Social Tariff was listed at £13.99 per month with 30 Mbit/s average speed in England.

records.f: Delayed repair compensation was £10.34 per calendar day after two full working days without full repair.

records.f: Missed appointment compensation was £32.31 per missed appointment.

records.f: Delayed new-service start compensation was £6.46 for each calendar day of delay.

records.f: Bill credit should normally be provided no later than 30 calendar days after the qualifying event is resolved or dated.
records.g: Payment timing cannot be inferred without account evidence.

records.f: Simultaneous loss of landline and broadband yields one compensation payment under the scheme.
records.g: The rule is not proof of a dual-service outage at an address.

records.f: Mobile complaint-handling satisfaction was 61% in 2024.
records.g: Survey satisfaction is aggregate evidence, not parcel service quality.

records.f: Broadband complaint-handling satisfaction was 58% in 2024.
records.g: The industry measure cannot determine an individual provider case.

records.f: Landline complaint-handling satisfaction was 60% in 2024.
records.g: Aggregate satisfaction is not address-level reliability evidence.

records.f: Twenty-three per cent of broadband customers reported a reason to complain in 2024, versus 20% in 2022.
records.g: Survey incidence does not prove a complaint or fault at a parcel.

records.f: Plusnet broadband overall satisfaction was 91%, while TalkTalk was 77%.
records.g: Provider averages cannot rank service at a specific address.

records.f: Eighty-three per cent of broadband customers were satisfied with service speed.
records.g: Self-reported satisfaction is not measured throughput at a parcel.

records.f: Seventy-three per cent of standalone broadband customers were satisfied with value for money, up from 62% in 2022.
records.g: Value perception is not an address-specific price or availability result.

records.f: Average broadband and landline call waiting time was 2 minutes 1 second in 2024, 13 seconds higher than 2023.
records.g: Industry waiting time does not describe an individual support interaction.

records.f: Broadband and landline orders took 11 days on average, and 73% were delivered by the agreed date in 2024.
records.g: Industry averages do not prove installation timing for an address.

records.f: Providers paid more than £63 million under automatic compensation in 2024, down from £67 million in 2023.
records.g: Total payouts do not establish an individual claim or outage.

records.f: The May snapshot totalled 837,340 contracted premises and 256,680 built contracted premises.
